youtube.title: Why One Semicolon Breaks Rust Code (Statements vs Expressions) 🦀 | Rust Day 10 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Statements vs expressions in Rust: why one extra semicolon breaks your function. Rust Day 10 of the Zero to Pro series.

📌 In this short:
✅ Statements do something (let y = 6;), expressions produce a value (5 + 6, a block, a function call)
✅ A block { } is an expression: its last line WITHOUT a semicolon is its value
✅ Add ; to that last line and the function returns () instead: error E0308, "remove this semicolon"

💻 Code from the video:
fn plus_one(x: i32) → i32 {
    x + 1
}
(YouTube won't show the real arrow: type → as a minus sign then a greater-than sign)

📖 Learn more: https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch03-03-how-functions-work.html
⏭️ Tomorrow: if / else

Follow for a new Rust lesson every day at 10 AM IST, from zero to pro 🦀

scenes.say: Add one semicolon, and this Rust function stops compiling. Here's why.

scenes.heading: A block has a value
scenes.say: A statement does something but gives no value, like let x equals three. An expression gives a value. Here, x plus one has no semicolon, so it's the value of the whole block. So y becomes four.
scenes.captions: A statement does something but gives no value, like let x = 3; An expression gives a value. Here, x + 1 has no semicolon, so it's the value of the whole block. So y becomes 4.

scenes.heading: Two kinds of code
scenes.say: So Rust code has two kinds of pieces. Statements, like let, or a function definition. And expressions: math, function calls, and even whole blocks.
scenes.captions: So Rust code has two kinds of pieces. Statements, like let, or a function definition. And expressions: math, function calls, and even whole blocks.

scenes.heading: Functions work the same
scenes.say: A function body is a block too. x plus one, with no semicolon, is what plus one returns. So plus one of five gives six.
scenes.captions: A function body is a block too. x + 1, with no semicolon, is what plus_one returns. So plus_one(5) gives 6.

scenes.heading: Common mistake
scenes.sub: a semicolon on the last line
scenes.say: Now the classic mistake: a semicolon after x plus one.
scenes.captions: Now the classic mistake: a semicolon after x + 1.

scenes.heading: Mismatched types
scenes.caption: remove this semicolon
scenes.say: The semicolon turns it into a statement, so the function returns nothing, written as empty parentheses, instead of an i32. Rust even says: remove this semicolon.
scenes.captions: The semicolon turns it into a statement, so the function returns nothing, written as (), instead of an i32. Rust even says: remove this semicolon.

scenes.heading: Fixed
scenes.say: Delete it, and it compiles again: y equals six.
scenes.captions: Delete it, and it compiles again: y = 6.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.say: Recap: statements give no value, expressions do, and a block's last line without a semicolon is its value.
